NVDA.short: On November 22, 2026, Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and director, effective immediately. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, stays as CFO. An independent committee's investigation into reports of a foreign intelligence effort targeting Huang will continue.

AMD.short: On November 18, 2026, AMD's board amended the company's bylaws, effective immediately. The changes add stricter procedures and disclosure rules for stockholder director nominations and proposals, let the company disregard noncompliant nominee votes, require non-white proxy cards, and update the legal forum rules.

short.AMD: Most coverage is opinion, but one event stands out: a Hunterbrook Media report alleged AMD kept supplying firmware to a blacklisted Chinese server maker, and the stock fell 7.7% on Nov. 19. AMD denies wrongdoing, and a law firm has opened an investigation. Articles disagree on the stock, with some funds selling while others buy, though Q3 data center revenue rose 97%.
short.NVDA: Nearly all of these articles are opinion pieces, but they describe one main event: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after an 11-day absence, and the stock jumped about 31% in a day before partly giving it back. This matters because his return eased key-person risk, yet probes into his conduct, an SEC accounting review and governance doubts remain. Strong Q3 results (103% revenue growth) are cited, but writers disagree on whether the stock is cheap or risky.
short.META: These articles are all opinion pieces, so no new company event is reported. They draw on Meta's Q3 2026 results, citing 26% ad revenue growth, higher ad impressions and prices, and wide advertiser use of AI tools. They disagree on the outlook: one stresses strong ad demand, while another flags heavy AI spending, negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion and large legal charges.
